item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I quite like this. This is foundation coldness in its most concentrated form. This item is aggressively inhumane, and the clinical matter in which the Foundation devises these procedures to make use of its properties are golden.

Developing a brain blender so they can keep their writhing organ farm from screaming is incredible, especially without the document belying any sense of remorse or disgust from anyone involved. In addition, said brain-blending likely means that the subject isn't even feeling any pain until the brain forms again, meaning that the procedure is actually *more* humane, while remaining just as horrifying and detached in practice.

Worth noting is that if there were any way to just lock it in a box, then this procedure would likely set off every one of the ethics committee's alarm bells. However, since somebody has to strapped into the nightmare organ farm no matter what anyway, the Foundation might as well steal some helpful bits.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
O5 Oversight

Overwatch?

In any event, it's an interesting experiment for a written document… but it becomes an exercise in cruelty st the half of it, and there is little or no interest on the item proper, it's anomaly exploitation and application only. I wouldn't mind it as much as I do (I'd probably have ended up thinking this was cruel, yet useful, if there wasn't so much bloody cruelty going on here. It reads precisely as an essay on clinical cruelty would, its main hook the gore and pragmatic, almost flippant approach shown by the Foundation personnel.

Altogether, I don't know what to make of it. might benefit from a shorter, straighter delivery; or maybe not, since I'm probably being a stick in the mud here.

Neutral vote for the bloody cruelty, redundancy intended.

item.content:encoded:
I think the tone and content of the emails is perfect. People who work with disgusting things all day do become desensitised or develop a cheery persona to cover their disgust. If you were a senior Foundation researcher, you'd either be jaded and cynical as hell, or jauntily keeping a brave face the whole time.

Plus, the machiney tinge to the engineers department is brilliant: utterly perfect large organisation. It wouldn't be quite as good without the contrasted doctor.

Finally, being all "Oh God what are we doing we're such bastards" followed by [REDACTED] found dead in his office would be too deep'n'edgy. Item is more hideous by contrast.

item.title: Possible answer for the pain
item.content:encoded:
A possible explanation for the pain:

If any of you have kids, there's a readily apparent source for the pain - growing pains. I know that after any sort of rigorous exercise, what is described in the article is an exaggerated form of what my kid goes through.

Now… imagine that happening constantly, all over the body.

Nice work JonnyD.

item.title: Object Classes
item.content:encoded: There really shouldn't be any reason for an SCP to have dual object classes. Please choose one and stick with it.

item.title: Re: Threat Diamond
item.content:encoded:
I figured they'd make a bit of effort to find a way to block whatever causes the endless screaming. If they can keep the holder from suffering without diminishing his/her mental capacity, then they could end up with an agent who regenerates from anything.

Of course, they could just try and fail. Nothing wrong with that.

item.title: Re: Threat Diamond
item.content:encoded:
I've made the change you suggested. I'm new to the threat diamond and I wasn't sure if it warranted a level 4. It's not dangerous to be around or near or even to touch so long as you don't let it touch your bare skin, and it's certainly not actively trying to kill anyone. But reading over the descriptions again, I think you're right, that it does kill you dead (eventually), so it should be a class 4.

I hadn't thought of experiments with painkillers as opposed to sedatives. To be honest the exact nature of what SCP-596 inflicts upon the subjects that makes then scream for the rest of their lives is perhaps the only mysterious element. I guess I see the foundation as being more interested in what they can get out of it.

Since you're using the threat diamond:

This should really be a Level 4 Physical Threat - you don't come away from touching it severely maimed, you come away from touching it dead.

Also, has anyone tried dosing the person holding the statue with lots of painkillers to see if they're screaming due to physical pain instead of some kind of mental effect?

item.title: SCP-596
item.content:encoded:
I've had a bit of a hiatus since my first 3 SCP creations, but I found some spare time and had an idea rattling round my head.

I figured that this would be a good deterrent against tomb robbers. Try and steal it and it'll subject you to an eternity of agony. If someone try's to take it off you, you die and they end up trapped in agony. No matter how many times you kill the person, they just grow back.

I guess the only way out is to destroy the statue itself, but I think the Foundation would find an endless supply of blood and organs too good to pass up. Obviously they could practically get that from the class D's anyway, but this way they can make copies of rare blood and organs.

And I know that a Foundation ethics committee might sound like an oxymoron, but since the site is about horror, what job could be more horrible than trying to answer the ethical questions that Foundation activities raise.
